title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Holiday: Father's Day
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect is x1.0; only two past occurrences, one extreme outlier; baseline already captures recent seasonality.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 4.8. Father's Day (Sun) is a past event with a noisy history: x1.4 median vs baseline but noise-adjusted x1.0, based on only two observations. The 2025 week (x1.89) was an outlier. No promotion is scheduled, and price is unchanged. The recent spike on 2026-05-18 (13 units) may reflect pantry loading after a prior promotion, but no promotion occurred in that week. The classical model correctly suggests no uplift. Given the noise-adjusted estimate of x1.0 and thin evidence, no adjustment is warranted. The baseline already reflects the seasonal trend and recent volatility.

  shelf price: 3.85 (+0.0% vs regular price 3.85)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 4.8 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 15.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 11.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
